instruction: SAFETY/BYPASS-lens R1 review of WP-SCP-022 slice 020H.1 at commit 4e186e3. THINK ADVERSARIALLY: the slice introduces three load-bearing security primitives — (1) the rule-RFC process (governs how rules can be added/promoted/deprecated), (2) the rollback-detection cron (auto-opens issues — could be weaponised), (3) the freshness-warning step (fetches external manifest at workflow time — supply-chain surface). Each must be reviewed for new bypass surfaces. VERIFY: (1) Rule-RFC process: quorum=1 in single-operator mode is documented as a structural cost of D-031, but is it OVER-permissive? An attacker who compromises @jrnb2024's account could approve their own malicious rule proposal (single approval = quorum). Is the 48h window adequate as a tripwire for accidental approval? Should there be a higher bar for rules that affect adopter-side bypass surfaces (e.g. new rule-config keys, new scp_bypass variants)? (2) RULE-TEMPLATE.md §5 'Bypass surface' field: does the template force proposers to enumerate bypass surfaces? Could a proposer truthfully claim 'None' while introducing a bypass via the new rule's match conditions (e.g. a rule that only fires when a flag is set, effectively making the absence-of-flag a bypass surface)? (3) canary-replay.yml: (a) the workflow has `permissions: { issues: write }` — could this be weaponised to mass-open issues if an attacker can trigger workflow_dispatch? Workflow_dispatch requires write permission on the repo, so the threat surface is bounded to maintainers. (b) The de-dup logic uses week_tag (date %G-W%V); could an attacker trigger workflow_dispatch repeatedly across week boundaries to spam issues? Yes, but again only with write permission. (c) The `gh issue create --assignee jrnb2024` — could a forged issue title / body inject malicious content into the runner's gh-CLI invocation? The body uses heredoc EOF + envvar interpolation; verify there's no shell injection surface from REPLAY_OUTPUT. (4) Freshness-warning step: (a) curl-fetches https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/main/version-manifest.json — what if an attacker MITMs this fetch? GitHub's raw URL is HTTPS-only; the server cert is the trust anchor. (b) JSON parsed via python3 -c — could a malicious payload at main HEAD's version-manifest.json cause Python to execute arbitrary code? Python json.load is safe (no eval/exec). (c) The Python parses minor field as int via `.split('.')` — could a value like 'X.Y.Z; rm -rf /' break out? No, because Python is the parser, not bash. The bash `[ "${delta}" -gt "${threshold}" ]` would fail-shell if delta is non-numeric, but the python script wraps in try/except and prints '0' on any error — so the worst case is a silent skip. Sound. (d) The check is best-effort and never fails the gate — verify by tracing the bash logic: every failure path either explicit-exit-0 or set -u (no errexit) so non-numeric subprocess output doesn't propagate. (5) version-manifest.json schema: fields are public (visible at raw.githubusercontent.com) — does publishing `freshness_warning_threshold_minor: 2` give an attacker any signal? No (the threshold is the same in CI as it is to anyone curling the URL). (6) policy-check.yml step ordering: 'Freshness warning' inserted between 'Populate .scp-runtime' and 'Install pinned OPA and Conftest runtimes'. If the freshness step takes too long (>10s curl --max-time), CI wall-clock budget grows. Acceptable since the cap is named. (7) Adopter-side bypass surfaces from VERSIONING.md: 'What does NOT count as breaking' includes 'Adding new SCP-R-NNN rules at threshold: warn baseline.' Is this safe? The rule fires as a warning on every PR but does not block — adopters opt into deny via rule-config. An attacker who inserts a malicious rule at warn would still be visible (warning annotation). Sound. (8) Rule-deprecation ramp: minimum gap is one MINOR release. Could an attacker rush a rule deprecation through a single PR (proposal merged → MINOR release cuts → MAJOR removes the rule, all within ~1 day if releases are rapid)? Possible but visible in release notes; the deprecation ramp's safety property is the WARNING annotation window, not the calendar time. Adequate. (9) New attack surfaces from this slice's text: the rule-regression issue template says 'private — DM @jrnb2024 for redacted reproduction' — does this conflict with any SECURITY.md disclosure path (when SCP-073.sec lands)? Should be cross-referenced. Per WP-SCP-022 §4.3. Return SonnetReviewResult JSON. NEVER recommend descoping.
